    People also ask
    What is the main purpose of the WHO?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The
    World Health Organization (WHO) is the United Nations’ specialized agency for international public health, founded in 1948 to promote health, keep the world safe, and serve the vulnerable. Its main purpose is to coordinate global health efforts, set international health standards, manage health emergencies, and promote universal health care. 
    Key functions and purposes of the WHO include: 
    • Directing and Coordinating Global Health: Acting as the lead authority on international health within the UN system.
    • Preventing & Controlling Disease: Fighting both communicable diseases (like HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis, and Ebola) and non-communicable diseases (like cancer and heart disease)
      .
    • Emergency Response: Leading global action against health emergencies, crises, and pandemic threats.
    • Setting Norms and Standards: Developing international health regulations, monitoring health trends, and creating evidence-based policies.
    • Promoting Health Equity: Working to ensure that all people achieve the highest possible level of health, regardless of race, religion, or economic condition. 
    The WHO is composed of 194 member states, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
